biography.plain_text: Thomas Bscher is a German property developer and former private banker based in Cologne. A grandson of financier Robert Pferdmenges, he became a personally liable partner at Sal. Oppenheim. His subsequent property business restores historic buildings, including Berlin’s Haus Cumberland and Frankfurt’s Villa Sander, adapting them for contemporary commercial use.

long_biography.plain_text:
Thomas Bscher helped turn the McLaren F1 from a road car into an endurance racer. Alongside Ray Bellm, he approached McLaren about competing in the international GT series. He then shared the 1995 championship with John Nielsen: two race victories and consistent finishes secured their title.

As president of Bugatti, Bscher faced a different challenge: getting the Veyron into production. Working with technical director Wolfgang Schreiber, his team reassessed the project’s technical and financial feasibility and established a realistic manufacturing timetable. Production began in 2005 at the new Molsheim workshop, bringing the ambitious supercar programme to the road.

Production began in 2005 at the new Molsheim workshop, bringing the ambitious supercar programme to the road.
